belief: I'm losing my mind, and nothing can be done.
origins: Noticing memory or thinking decline is frightening, especially when family history or a diagnosis is involved. Fear and hopelessness can lead to avoiding doctors, therapy, and support.
teaches: “The Spirit helps us in our weakness.” “Cast all your anxiety on Him, because He cares for you.” “Plans fail for lack of counsel, but with many advisers they succeed.” Some memory problems are treatable or manageable, such as those from sleep problems, medications, depression, thyroid, vitamin deficiencies, or stress, and even progressive conditions can be eased with support, safety planning, and care. Get evaluated. Nothing can be done is rarely the truth. Even if the mind fades, God’s hold on you does not: “You hold my right hand” (Psalm 73:23).
self_statements: It is only going to get worse.
errors: Believing my mind is either fine or gone.
Feeling afraid and concluding there is nothing to do.
questions: Have I been evaluated by a doctor?
What treatable causes could be checked?
What helps me function better now?
Who can help me plan and keep me safe?
What does Scripture say about God’s hold on me?
truth: I will get evaluated, use every help available, and plan with those I trust. Even if my mind changes, God’s hold on me does not. Nothing is too hard for His care.
log: Each month, note one step taken: an appointment, a plan, or a conversation.
prayer: Lord, I am afraid for my mind. Guide me to good care, give me peace, and hold me in Your hand whatever comes. Amen.
